capabilities: Browse knowledge bases as a card wall grouped by real folders
Open a per-knowledge-base file tree mirroring the native explorer
Reorder and move cards, groups, and files by drag and drop
Share custom sort, pin, and hide state with the native file explorer
Render custom callouts in Live Preview and Reading view
disambiguation: Not a home-page dashboard plugin; it is a scoped replacement view for browsing vault folders and their files.
extras: The plugin UI is currently in Chinese; commands are listed with Chinese names. Settings from an older 'kb-home' plugin id are not migrated. Detailed known limitations are documented, including callout rendering quirks in Reading view and missing file-menu events in the scoped tree.
motivation: The README's 'Why' section says the author built it to split the single native file tree into two levels: a card wall of knowledge bases and a per-knowledge-base tree.
problem: Obsidian's native file explorer shows every folder in one tree, which becomes unwieldy when the vault holds many separate projects.

relations.evidence: The sort/pin/hide engine in src/core/ is adapted from Flexplorer (MIT, by kh4f).
Callout support is based on the earlier admonition-blocks implementation.

summary: Two-level knowledge-base browser that turns the home view into a card wall of folders, each opening a file tree scoped to that knowledge base.
